label: Late original-phase input of t/m/d/v/k/s/z/a/r, with a per-token position threshold
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at positions 4-8, when the current input is one of nine letters. Each letter has its own earliest position: t from position 4, m/d from 5, v/k from 6, s/z/a from 7, and r only at 8. Read as a single feature, it looks like input token identity plus how far into the sequence we are, with each token needing a different position to cross the threshold. Activation is larger for later positions and roughly follows the token ordering t > m,d > v,k > s,z,a > r. The top activations (about 4.3) are t at position 7-8, and t carries 37% of the activation mass. Within a position it is almost exactly position-locked: whenever the token-and-position condition holds, the feature fires (precision about 1.0 per cell). It does not fire at positions 0-3, at the delimiter (2 stray activations), in the copy phase, or on any other token. It does not depend on L, earlier tokens, or the first token. Dev F1 0.99, mass recall 0.9995.

issues: Minor overclaim: the explanation says every token-and-position cell has precision of about 1.0, but at the threshold cells it is lower. a at t=7 has precision 0.81 and s/z/a at t=7 together have 0.92 (dev). The cells above the threshold do have precision 1.0.

Boundary leakage: r at t=7 fires in 19% of cases, all at very low activation (about 0.01-0.05 relative). This accounts for most of the 1196 test misses, which hold about 0.0% of the activation mass. It is a soft edge to the threshold, not a missing class.
Test false positives (1375) are mostly s/z/a at t=7 that do not fire. This is the same soft threshold edge and carries negligible mass.

Other claims checked out. The feature never fires in the copy phase (0 of 2.7M steps) and fires at the delimiter only twice. It is silent at t=0-3 and essentially silent on other tokens (n/h/u about 30 each). Its mass share is t 37%, m 22%, d 20%. t at t>=7 has precision 1.0. The apparent dependence on L is just position: t>=4 requires L>=5.
Reported test scores reproduced: precision 0.991, recall 0.992, F1 0.992, mass recall 0.9995.
